# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 59 (Bu-Vb Pc59)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc59
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 59
**Title (English, from literature):** Using assigned property that has not been relinquished
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 59 (titled *Vikappana*, translated as "Using assigned property that has not been relinquished") is an expiation rule within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule specifies that a monk incurs a *pācittiya* offense if he uses robe-cloth or monastic requisites whose ownership has been shared or transferred (*vikappana*) to a fellow monastic without the second party first relinquishing it or granting permission [Vajirananavarorasa]. In monastic practice, an exception applies when the two monks are intimate friends, though formal acknowledgment remains recommended [Vajirananavarorasa]. As noted in the *Samantapāsādikā*, the tradition developed mechanisms of direct and mediated assignment (*sammukhāvikappanā* and *parammukhāvikappanā*) to enable members of the Saṅgha to maintain access to necessary requisites such as robes and bowls despite rigorous monastic restrictions [Hüsken 1997].

The rule has wide parallels across Vinaya traditions, corresponding to the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Pācittiya 59) and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 140) of the Theravāda tradition, as well as parallel pācittiya rules in the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsāṃghika codes preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions.
